t2116.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Zayd ibn Arqam al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī as a well-known Companion whose first battle was the Trench, whose confirmation God sent down in Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn; he died in 66 or 68.
as: فأنزل الله - تعالى - تصديق زيد بن أرقم
God revealed confirmation of Zayd ibn Arqam’s account.
البراء, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
سل زيد بن أرقم، فإنه خير مني وأعلم.
Ask Zayd ibn Arqam, for he is better than I and knows more.
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
إن الله قد صدقك يا زيد
God has confirmed that you spoke the truth, Zayd.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
Your ear retained it, young man.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
God has confirmed that you spoke the truth.

t5122.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī, a well-known mukhaḍram, trustworthy and devout, who settled in Kufa and died in year 74 or later.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
A Kufan Successor, trustworthy, who lived in the Jāhiliyyah.
كان أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرضون بعمرو بن ميمون
The Prophet's Companions approved of ʿAmr ibn Maymūn.
يا عمرو بن ميمون قد كنت أظنك من أفقه أهل هذه القرية
Ibn Masʿūd: ʿAmr, I thought you among the most learned of this town.
حج عمرو بن ميمون ستين من بين حجة وعمرة
He went on sixty pilgrimages, counting both ḥajj and ʿumrah.
He went on a hundred pilgrimages, counting both ḥajj and ʿumrah.
al-ʿIjlī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
A trustworthy Kufan Successor who lived in the Jāhiliyyah.
ابن إسحاق, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
The Companions used to commend him.
ابن معين والنسائي وغيرهما, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
Ibn Maʿīn, al-Nasāʾī and others declared him trustworthy.
al-Nasāʾī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī

t7937.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Abū Isḥāq, who transmits from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, as unknown and of the seventh generation.

t8020.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū Jaʿfar al-Farrāʾ al-Kūfī as trustworthy, of the fourth generation; his name is given variously as Salmān, Kaysān or Ziyād; cited by al-Bukhārī and al-Nasāʾī.

t8244.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records that Abū ʿUthmān, teacher of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād, is Muslim ibn Yasār; otherwise he is unknown, of the third generation.

t8442.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists another Abū Wahb al-Kalāʿī, acceptable, of the fourth generation, and marks it as a distinguishing note.

t8558.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ḥabība bint ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh al-Asadiyya, whose mother was Umm Ḥabība bint Abī Sufyān. She had Companionship, emigrated with her parents to Abyssinia, and is said to have been born there.

t8697.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hind bint Sharīk al-Baṣriyyah, acceptable, of the third generation.

t952.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Rasʿanī, Abū al-Faḍl, also called al-Rāsī, as truthful and a memorizer, of the eleventh generation.
